stories.title: GPT-6.2 Astra undercuts rivals on price by up to 600%, but early reviews are mixed
stories.summary: GPT-6.2 Astra, now the #2 frontier model by some measures, is reportedly 20-600% cheaper on benchmark costs than rivals, but early testers are split on how it performs; the smaller Sol variant is expected to be the daily workhorse.
stories.more: A roundup from Latent Space's AINews newsletter covers the release of GPT-6.2 Astra and a smaller companion model, Sol. It says Astra lowers benchmark costs significantly, by a reported 20% to 600% compared to earlier models, while ranking as the #2 frontier model by some measure. Early testers reportedly disagree on what Astra is actually like to work with day to day. Sol, the smaller sibling, is expected to become the more commonly used 'workhorse' model despite Astra's headline position. The excerpt doesn't specify which lab released these models, exact pricing, or benchmark details.

stories.title: New benchmark Breath-Dx tests AI disease screening via e-nose breath analysis
stories.summary: Breath-Dx is a new time-series classification benchmark for diagnosing disease from exhaled breath using electronic nose sensors, aiming to let machine-learning methods be compared under realistic conditions like sensor drift.
stories.more: Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive way to screen for disease by analyzing exhaled breath. Progress in the field has been limited by a lack of systematic benchmarks that compare machine-learning methods under realistic conditions, especially sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode. Most prior studies used small, private datasets with inconsistent protocols, making results hard to compare and slowing progress. Breath-Dx is introduced as a benchmark meant to close that gap, though the excerpt doesn't detail its dataset size or which models were evaluated.

stories.title: AURA 2.0 lets streaming video AI speak first instead of waiting to be asked
stories.summary: AURA 2.0 is a streaming video language model that can initiate conversation on its own, spotting moments in a live video feed worth discussing instead of only responding when prompted.
stories.more: Most AI video assistants only respond when prompted, staying silent even when something in the stream is worth commenting on. AURA 2.0 introduces Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which lets the model identify topics worth discussing as a video stream unfolds and speak up at an appropriate moment rather than waiting for a question. The paper describes this as one of three core upgrades over the original AURA system. Details on the other two upgrades and on evaluation results aren't given in the excerpt.

stories.title: Multi-Branch Transformer scales models by branching instead of going wider or deeper
stories.summary: A new paper proposes the Multi-Branch Transformer, which runs parallel branches of Transformer blocks after shared initial layers and fuses their outputs, as an alternative to simply widening or deepening models.
stories.more: Transformer language models are typically scaled by making blocks wider or stacking more of them. The Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT) instead processes input through shared initial layers, runs independently parameterized branches of sequential blocks in parallel, and fuses their outputs before shared final layers. The authors say they study three MBT variants at comparable training compute. The excerpt doesn't give benchmark results or say how the variants compare to standard scaling in practice.

stories.title: Suno adds AI-generated video and lip-synced visuals to its music, calls it 'Visuals'
stories.summary: Suno launched 'Visuals', a feature that turns songs made on its AI music platform into AI-generated video clips with automatic lip-sync to the lyrics, or into prompt-generated images for thumbnails and artwork.
stories.more: Suno, previously known purely as an AI music generator, has introduced a feature called Visuals that extends it into image and video generation. Visuals can turn a Suno song into an AI-generated video clip that automatically lip-syncs to the track's lyrics. It can also generate standalone images from text prompts, intended for use as thumbnails or album artwork. Neither report gives a rollout timeline or pricing for the new feature.

stories.title: Smell startup Osmo says its AI nose matches human scent-identification accuracy
stories.summary: AI startup Osmo claims its 'foundation model' for smell, trained on data from about 30 human sniffers cross-referenced with chemical analysis, can identify odors as well as a person can.
stories.more: Osmo is building what it calls the world's first foundation model for smell. To train it, a team of roughly 30 experienced human sniffers works through odor samples near Newark Airport, writing descriptive notes like 'nutty', 'peachy', and 'marine' that are cross-referenced with chemical analysis. The company claims its resulting AI system can identify smells as accurately as a human nose. The excerpt doesn't detail the model's architecture, what products it will power, or how its accuracy was measured.

stories.title: Lovable pivots from vibe-coding apps to helping users run vibe-coded businesses
stories.summary: Swedish startup Lovable, known for driving the vibe-coded app boom, is shifting its product two years after launch to help users operate businesses built with AI-generated ('vibe-coded') code, not just build them.
stories.more: Lovable, a Swedish startup, became a major driver of the 'vibe coding' boom, in which people build apps by describing them to AI rather than writing code by hand. Two years after its launch, the company is now shifting toward helping users run businesses built on vibe-coded software, rather than just helping them create the apps in the first place. The report frames this as a deliberate gear change for the company. It doesn't specify new product features, pricing, or a launch date for the shift.

stories.title: ForceHarness gives frozen frontier models a sense of touch for robot control
stories.summary: A new paper introduces ForceHarness, which feeds contact-force data to frozen, API-only frontier models in a form they can reason about, letting them guide robot manipulation tasks that rely on touch rather than vision alone.
stories.more: Frontier multimodal models can already control robots zero-shot from images, but many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images can't capture. Bringing force sensing to an API-only frozen model poses two challenges: contact dynamics change faster than the model can decide, so the system needs a control loop beneath the model, and the model can't interpret raw force streams on its own. ForceHarness addresses both by closing the fast loop separately and returning force information in a format the model can reason about. The excerpt doesn't specify which base models or robot platforms were tested.

stories.title: HN debates a travel blog's claim that AI search is killing its business
stories.summary: A blog post titled 'AI is killing All About Berlin' argues AI-powered search is destroying traffic to independent travel sites, and sparked a large Hacker News discussion with 346 comments.
stories.more: The post, titled 'AI is killing All About Berlin,' attributes the decline of the author's independent travel-information site to AI-powered search answering queries directly instead of sending clicks to original sources. It drew significant attention on Hacker News, reaching 375 points and 346 comments. The available excerpt doesn't include further detail on specific traffic numbers or which AI systems were blamed.
